article.headline: England battles Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi after failing to chase 300 runs
article.summary: England plays Sri Lanka in a pivotal one-day international tri-series match in Rawalpindi following a recent defeat against Pakistan.
article.body:
England enters today's match in Rawalpindi seeking a rebound after flunking a 300-plus run chase for the second time in three matches during Tuesday's loss to Pakistan. The batting lineup has shown significant inconsistency, shifting between positive performances and tame collapses that have defined their recent form. According to BBC reporting, Ben Duckett has experimented with six different opening partners in ODI cricket, with an average of 84.33 alongside Jacob Bethell across three stands, compared to a 64.50 average when paired with Banton.

For England, the stakes are rising as the team faces a potential bottom-place finish in the tri-series standings at the halfway mark. With zero points currently on the board, today’s game against Sri Lanka is effectively a must-win scenario to avoid a significant deficit in the series. The Guardian notes that the squad's tendency to oscillate between strong starts and poor finishes has raised concerns following a year that was otherwise marked by largely positive results in 2026.

Technical analysis from Cricviz's Rufus Bullough highlights the ongoing experimentation within the squad's top order. As England and Sri Lanka take to the field, both teams are under pressure to secure a win and climb away from the bottom of the table. The outcome of this match will determine the trajectory for the remainder of the series as teams look to rectify negative patterns and establish stability in their batting configurations.

news.title: عام / تنفيذ حُكم القتل تعزيرًا في أحد الجناة بمنطقة مكة المكرمة
news.og_title: عام / تنفيذ حُكم القتل تعزيرًا في أحد الجناة بمنطقة مكة المكرمة
news.og_desc:
جدة 08 جمادى الأولى 1448 هـ الموافق 19 أكتوبر 2026 م واس
    أصدرت وزارة الداخلية اليوم، بيانًا بشأن تنفيذ حُكم القتل تعزيرًا بأحد الجناة في منطقة مكة المكرمة، فيما يلي نصه:
    قال الله تعالى: "وَلَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ بَعْدَ إِصْلاحِهَا"، وقال تعالى: "وَلَا تَبْغِ الْفَسَادَ فِي الْأَرْضِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُفْسِدِينَ"، وقال تعالى: "وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْفَسَادَ"، وقال تعالى: "إِنَّمَا جَزَاء الَّذِينَ يُحَارِبُونَ اللّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَسَادًا أَن يُقَتَّلُوا أَوْ يُصَلَّبُوا أَوْ تُقَطَّعَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُم مِّنْ خِلافٍ أَوْ يُنفَوْا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ، ذَلِكَ لَهُمْ خِزْيٌ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَلَهُمْ فِي الآخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ".
    أقدم/ قيسمات جول -باكستاني الجنسية- على تهريب الهيروين المخدر إلى المملكة، وبفضل من الله تمكنت الجهات الأمنية من القبض على الجاني المذكور، وأسفر التحقيق معه عن توجيه الاتهام إليه بارتكاب الجريمة، وبإحالته إلى المحكمة المختصة؛ صدر بحقه حُكم يقضي بثبوت ما نُسب إليه وقتله تعزيرًا، وأصبح الحُكم نهائيًا بعد استئنافه ثم تأييده من المحكمة العليا، وصدر أمرٌ ملكي بإنفاذ ما تقرر شرعًا.
    وتم تنفيذ حُكم القتل تعزيرًا بالجاني/ قيسمات جول -باكستاني الجنسية- يوم الاثنين 8 / 5 / 1448هـ الموافق 19 / 10 / 2026م بمنطقة مكة المكرمة.
    ووزارة الداخلية إذ تعلن ذلك لتؤكد للجميع حرص حكومة المملكة العربية السعودية على حماية أمن المواطن والمقيم من آفة المخدرات، وإيقاع أشد العقوبات المقررة نظامًا بحق مهربيها ومروجيها، لما تسببه من إزهاق للأرواح البريئة، وفساد جسيم في النشء والفرد والمجتمع، وانتهاك لحقوقهم، وهي تحذر في الوقت نفسه كل من يقدم على ذلك بأن العقاب الشرعي سيكون مصيره.
    واللّه الهادي إلى سواء السبيل.

news.title: New Zealand study 'incredible' Sooryavanshi ahead of T20I series, says Kiwi pacer Duffy
news.og_title: New Zealand study 'incredible' Sooryavanshi ahead of T20I series, says Kiwi pacer Duffy
news.og_desc: New Zealand have studied India's teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi ahead of the five-match T20I series and are confident that home conditions will test the 15-year-old, Kiwi pacer Jacob Duffy said on Tuesday. Sooryavanshi has taken world cricket by storm with his explosive batting, rewriting records in the Indian Premier League (IPL) before becoming the youngest player to represent India in men's international cricket during the T20I series in England in July. Now, a part of India's T20I team which will play a five-match T20I series in New Zealand, Sooryavanshi will be tested by the pace and bounce. "First of all, he's an incredible talent. Obviously, he's taken the IPL by storm and what's amazing, he strikes it so hard but he does it so consistently," Duffy told reporters, as per Reuters. "He's striking at 250 (strike-rate) every game and he's not missing out very often. So that's incredible in itself. I think he played in England, so conditions will be a little bit different for him, so that's obviously one thing for him to be challenged with. We've certainly had a good scouting session on him and got our plans as to what we want to do to him," Duffy added. After a relatively quiet start against England, Sooryavanshi announced himself on the international stage by becoming the youngest player to score a half-century in men's international cricket, smashing an 18-ball fifty against Zimbabwe. He was also part of India's gold medal-winning campaign at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, where the team clinched the men's T20 cricket title. The opening T20I of the five-match series will be played at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Thursday, with India's batters expected to face a different challenge on New Zealand's traditionally seam-friendly pitches. Duffy said he had spoken to Hagley Oval's head groundsman about the surface and was hoping for conditions that would assist the bowlers. "He's from Invercargill, so he's promised me a little bit of bounce," said Duffy, who was born in Lumsden on New Zealand's South Island. "As long as it's not Hyderabad, I'm happy," Duffy added, as per Reuters. The T20I series will be the first leg of India's tour of New Zealand, which also includes five one-day internationals and two Tests. India last toured the country in November 2022 for three ODIs and three T20Is. Duffy, who won the Sir Richard Hadlee Medal as New Zealand's top player in 2025, has enjoyed a productive year, reaching the final of the T20 World Cup in India before winning the IPL with Royal Challengers Bengaluru. The 31-year-old made his Test debut last year and is eager to strengthen his case for a place in New Zealand's red-ball side ahead of a four-Test tour of Australia. "I've played four tests in my life. I get up for any test. There's something special about them," he said, according to Reuters. Duffy missed New Zealand's mid-year tour of England and the one-off Test against Ireland to be with his wife for the birth of their first child. (ANI)
